Character sprite sheet for a mid-1990s 16-bit home console role-playing adventure game, authentic hand-pixelled pixel art. The attached references only show the costume and body proportions (first image) and the leg poses of a walk cycle (second image): keep the costume and the poses, but drawing style, resolution and palette follow this description. Each sprite frame is TINY: about 24 art pixels wide and 32 art pixels tall, enlarged without smoothing so every art pixel is a crisp, clearly visible square block of the same size on one regular grid (about 6 by 6 image pixels); no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no texture noise, no glow. One sprite palette of at most 15 colours: 3 shades of dark green for cap and vest, 3 reds for the scarf, 2 browns for the satchel, 2 tans for the parcel, cream for the shirt and the face stripe, 3 greys for the fur, a brass-yellow pixel for the cap button, and a dark coloured outline (very dark brown-purple, not pure black) around the whole figure. Chunky, cute proportions like a console role-playing game hero sprite: big head about one third of the height, short stout body, short legs; the face reduced to a dark eye pixel, a dark nose tip and the white face stripe. Side view facing right.

Layout: two rows on a fully transparent background, all figures at exactly the same scale, evenly spaced with clear empty space between them, the feet of each row on one baseline. Top row: 6 frames of a walk cycle walking to the right, each frame a distinct leg and arm position: contact (front leg forward), down, passing (legs together), up, contact with the other leg forward, passing; the parcel stays under the near arm, the scarf end swings behind. Bottom row: 4 frames standing still facing right: 1 standing relaxed, mouth closed; 2 the same pose with eyes closed (blink); 3 talking, mouth open, the free paw raised in a small gesture; 4 standing relaxed, turned three-quarters towards the viewer.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Location screen of a mid-1990s 16-bit home console role-playing adventure game, authentic hand-pixelled tile-based pixel art. The native screen is only 256 pixels wide: the whole picture is built from crisp square art pixels of one size on one regular grid (each art pixel a clearly visible square block, about 4 by 4 image pixels), as if the tiny console screen were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no mixed pixel sizes, no soft airbrushed gradients. Limited palette of about 100 colours. Every material uses only 3 to 5 flat shades with clean pixel clusters: light-grey stone with blue-violet shadows, warm brown wood planks, dark slate roof, mossy grey rocks, white lighthouse with one red band. Dark coloured outlines around every object (deep purple-brown and dark navy, never pure black), bright one-pixel highlight edges on the lit side. Sky in clear stepped horizontal colour bands: dark indigo at the top with a few single-pixel stars, violet, magenta-pink, a band of orange light at the horizon; low clouds as flat pixel shapes with two or three shades, a few short rows of ordered dithering only between the sky bands. The sea is drawn as horizontal stripes and short light dashes in deep blue and violet, with simple vertical stripe reflections of the orange horizon, the lit window, the lantern and the lighthouse lamp. Warm yellow light from the cottage window and the lantern glass, the lighthouse lamp only as a small glowing yellow spot without any beam or rays, no smoke from the chimney, no glow halos (light and smoke are animated separately in the game).

Side view with a fixed camera slightly above standing eye level, like a location screen in an adventure role-playing game. Composition (square image): the horizon lies at about 40% of the image height. The flat walkable top surface of the quay (stone slabs) is a wide horizontal band from about 55% to 72% of the image height across the whole width; below it the front wall of large stone blocks and dark water fill the bottom quarter, kept simple (a text box will cover it). The harbour-master's cottage stands on the left at the back edge of the quay and takes about a quarter of the image width. The lighthouse stands on its rocky headland on the right, its top at about 12% of the image height. The short wooden jetty leads from the quay into the water in the middle, the two small boats are moored beside it in the middle distance. Barrels, crates, the rope coil and the lantern on its wooden post stand along the back edge of the quay, the middle of the quay surface stays free for the characters to walk. Readable silhouettes, few big objects, friendly slightly stylised shapes. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not modern high-resolution pixel art with thousands of colours, no lens flare, no bloom, no light rays, no blurry gradients.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.
